Unity has acquired Synty Studios, the creators of the POLYGON asset line
Published by
admin
Tags:
Synty Studios
,
Unity
The Unity family is growing. The company
announced
the acquisition of New Zealand-based Synty Studios, a studio specializing in the development of low-poly 3D assets.
The financial terms and full details of the deal have not been disclosed, but it is known that in the future all assets from Synty Studios will appear in the Unity Spark library. As a reminder, this is an AI platform for game creation, with a closed beta test set to start by the end of the year.
Unity emphasized that Synty Studios will continue to operate under its own brand despite the acquisition. The company also promised that the acquisition will not impact the Synty Store, and the assets available there will remain accessible for use on third-party engines, including Unreal Engine and Godot.
Notably, not all Synty Studios employees will join the Unity team, only “the majority” will. The total number of employees has not been specified.
Synty Studios has been operating since 2014. During this time, they have created over 70,000 assets, but gained particular fame with their POLYGON series. Synty Studios’ assets have been used in games such as Dispatch and Tabletop Tavern.
